newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-TWO CLUB PRESIDENTS SUSPENDED IN BRAZIL SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TWO CLUB PRESIDENTS SUSPENDED IN BRAZIL SCANDAL.

text.p: Two leading Brazilian soccer club presidents were suspended on Friday in the wake of a corruption scandal, the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) said.

Mario Cesar Petraglia, president of Atletico Paranaense, and Alberto Duarib, president of Corinthians, were banned from any soccer-related activity as a preventative measure, said CBF spokesman Nelson Borges.
Ivens Mendes, the president of the CBF's refereeing department who resigned on Wednesday, was also suspended. The bans will last until an inquiry has been completed, Borges said.
The scandal erupted after Globo television played a recording of a telephone conversation which it said was between Mendes and Petraglia. The recording was sent in anonymously, Globo said.

The man identified as Mendes asked Petraglia for 25,000 Real ($23,600) and offered to ask a referee to give Petraglia's club Atletico a helping hand in a Copa Brasil match they were to play at home to Vasco da Gama.
He also told Petraglia to instruct his players to mark Vasco striker Edmundo tightly, adding: "He gets angry easily."
The man identified as Petraglia told Mendes in reply that his secretary would look after the matter.
Globo also played a tape of a conversation which it said was between Mendes and Duarib and which it claimed was evidence of an exchange of favours between the two.
CBF president Ricardo Teixeira said on Friday that the Copa Brasil, now at its semi-final stage, would carry on.

Atletico won the match in question, a second round, first leg game, 3-1. Edmundo, who has a record of sendings-off, and Atletico defender Andrei were both dismissed in the first half for fighting. Edmundo said: "It was a huge injustice."
Atletico went on to win the tie on aggregate but were subsequently knocked out in the quarter-finals by Corinthians, who lost 2-1 at home to Gremio in the first leg of a semi-final on Thursday night.

On Friday, Globo television carried a telephone interview with a man it identified as referee Walter Senra. He claimed to have been dropped in 1993 after refusing a request from Mendes to help make sure that the Remo club did not get promoted to the elite of the Brazilian championship.
The alleged request preceded a Serie B match involving the club from the northern city of Belem.

"He asked me, in fact almost demanded, that Remo should not qualify for the first division. I said I could do not do this because I'm not a striker and I don't score goals," the man identified as Senra said.
"I didn't do what he asked and as a result, I was removed from the Brazilian championship."
Reports published widely in the Brazilian media have alleged that Mendes is attempting to be elected to the Brazilian Congress and used money sent to him by clubs to help his election campaign.

They claimed he used the money to build football pitches in the state of Minas Gerais, where he is aiming to be elected, and showed billboards with his name. Mendes has admitted he received money but claimed it was all above board.
He has been quoted as saying: "What is wrong with me as a Brazilian citizen...who is trying to start a political career accepting help from my friends?"
